title: Batch-profile tradeoff lab: simulator & heuristics (INT8/FP8/4-bit)
content:
Purpose:
This is an experimental sandbox doc for a batch-profile-aware tradeoff simulator that helps recommend quantization choices (INT8 / FP8 / 4-bit) by workload class. The goal: give engineers quick, evidence-backed heuristics that balance cost, p95 latency, and end-task quality for common Redwood serving patterns.

Context & motivation:
- Existing spreadsheets focus on single-point cost comparisons (tokens * cost-per-token). They miss batch shape and latency SLO interactions.
- Quantization reduces GPU memory and per-token FLOPs but changes kernel performance and sometimes increases token-level CPU overhead for dequant/requant. That interplay is batch-size and sequence-length dependent.
- Need a simulator that: 1) models batching curves, 2) projects cost delta per 1M tokens, 3) estimates quality drift per eval set (ROUGE/EM/embedding-cosine), and 4) produces simple deployment recommendations.

High-level approach (simulator model):
1) Workload profile input (spreadsheet columns):
   - workload_name (string)
   - avg_prompt_len_tokens (int)
   - avg_resp_len_tokens (int)
   - request_rate_rps (float)
   - typical_batch_window_ms (int)  # window for server batching behavior
   - allowed_p95_latency_ms (int)
   - quality_metric (string, e.g., "embedding_cosine" | "rouge-l" | "exact_match")
   - baseline_quality_score (float)  # measured on baseline FP16 model

2) Model parameters (config, per model / per hw):
   - baseline_throughput_tokens_per_sec_fp16 (float)
   - int8_speedup_factor_over_fp16 (float)  # measured on sample kernel runs
   - fp8_speedup_factor_over_fp16 (float)
   - 4bit_speedup_factor_over_fp16 (float)
   - int8_quality_delta (pct)  # negative means quality drop relative to FP16
   - fp8_quality_delta (pct)
   - 4bit_quality_delta (pct)
   - additional_batch_overhead_ms (per_request_ms)  # queueing + batching overhead
   - fixed_request_cost_usd (float)  # infra per-request overhead (network, CPU)

3) Simulator output columns (spreadsheet will compute):
   - effective_batch_size (float) = estimate from request_rate, batch_window, and model latency
   - tokens_per_second_effective = baseline_throughput * effective_batch_scaling
   - projected_p95_latency_ms per quant mode = queueing_estimate + decode_time
   - projected_cost_per_1M_tokens_usd per quant mode = infra_cost + gpu_time_cost
   - projected_quality_score per quant mode = baseline_quality_score + quality_delta
   - decision = recommended quant mode (one of "FP16" | "INT8" | "FP8" | "4bit") with rationale string

Example formulas and heuristics (spreadsheet-friendly pseudo formulas):
   - effective_batch_size = max(1, min(max_possible_batch_by_gpu_mem, request_rate_rps * batch_window_ms / 1000))
   - gpu_time_ms = (total_tokens_per_request / baseline_tokens_per_sec_fp16) * (1 / speedup_factor_current_mode) * 1000
   - queueing_ms = ErlangC_approx(request_rate_rps, service_rate_rps) * 1000  # quick approx; spreadsheet uses simple util/(1-util) for util<0.8
   - projected_p95_latency_ms = queueing_ms + gpu_time_ms + additional_batch_overhead_ms
   - gpu_cost_per_ms_usd = (hourly_gpu_price_usd / 3600000) * concurrent_gpu_factor  # map time to $
   - cost_per_1M_tokens = sum_over_requests( gpu_cost + fixed_request_cost_usd ) scaled to 1M tokens

Quality modeling notes:
- We avoid modeling per-token perplexity changes; instead prefer end-task deltas from a small eval set per workload (10-50 prompts). Use embedding similarity or task-specific metric.
- Default quality deltas (placeholder) to tune from bench: INT8 -0.6% embedding cosine, FP8 -0.3%, 4-bit -1.5% (workload-dependent).
- Add columns for "uncertainty_pct" so recommendations propagate confidence.

Sample simulated rows (toy numbers):
- worklow_name: "support-bot"
  avg_prompt_len_tokens: 50
  avg_resp_len_tokens: 80
  request_rate_rps: 40
  batch_window_ms: 20
  allowed_p95_latency_ms: 300
  baseline_quality_score: 0.892 (embedding cosine)

Simulated outputs (toy):
- FP16: effective_batch_size=8, p95=250ms, cost/1M=480 USD, quality=0.892
- INT8: effective_batch_size=8, p95=220ms, cost/1M=320 USD, quality=0.886 (drop -0.6%)
- FP8: effective_batch_size=8, p95=230ms, cost/1M=340 USD, quality=0.889 (drop -0.3%)
- 4-bit: effective_batch_size=8, p95=200ms, cost/1M=210 USD, quality=0.877 (drop -1.5%)
Recommendation heuristic (spreadsheet rule):
  - If quality_drop > allowed_quality_loss_pct (workload-level), then exclude mode. Default allowed_quality_loss_pct = 0.5% for customer-facing content; 2% for internal search/embedding use-cases.
  - Among remaining modes, choose the one with lowest cost/1M that still meets p95 latency SLO.
  - If multiple modes tie on cost, pick one with smallest uncertainty_pct.

Edge cases and caveats:
- Very small batch sizes (effective_batch_size < 2) often eliminate INT8/FP8 speed advantages; the spreadsheet should display a warning and flip to a per-request latency-first recommendation.
- Long-context workloads (avg_resp_len + avg_prompt_len > 2k tokens) require memory-bound modeling: effective_batch_max may be lower; 4-bit memory wins may be larger here.
- Quantization sometimes changes temperature-dependent output distributions. For rated outputs (rating tasks) run small A/B evals before rollout.

Planned experiments to calibrate parameters (owners + rough timeline):
- Kernel-level bench (Marcus) 2 weeks: measure speedup factors for common models (Redwood-v1, RW-Chat-Base) on g5/gn5 like instances across seq lengths (64/256/1024). Record int8/fp8/4bit speedups.
- Quality evals (Leila) 1 week: run a 50-prompt eval per workload class (support, generation, summarization, embeddings) to estimate quality deltas and uncertainty.
- Queueing microbench (Ravi) 1 week: synthetic traffic generator to verify queueing model vs real server traces; derive simple util->queueing_ms mapping for spreadsheet.

Spreadsheet layout suggestion (tabs):
- inputs (workload rows + model/hw params)
- per-workload-sim (computed outputs and decisions per quant mode)
- calibration (bench numbers and raw results)
- rollout-guidance (text recommendations and runbook for canary A/B)

Quick-rollout recommendation template (for sales/SEs):
- Short: "Recommend INT8 for support-bot on g5.xlarge: saves ~33% on per-token cost and meets p95 300ms SLO; expected embedding cosine drop ~0.6% (run 5k prompt canary)."
- Include explicit canary checklist: traffic slice, metric thresholds, abort triggers (quality drop > 1% or latency p95 > SLO * 1.2).

Open TODOs (work in progress):
- Add a simple UI-friendly CSV export (tab-separated) that maps recommended rollout and canary config.
- Add a one-click "sensitivity sweep" that varies batch_window_ms and shows Pareto frontier.
- Decide default allowed_quality_loss_pct by workload class (ops decision).
- Incorporate Redwood Console metrics (p95 traces, token distributions) as a CSV ingestion path.

Notes to self / scratch ideas (informal):
- Could add an "opportunistic fallback" recommendation: e.g., use FP8 by default but fall back to FP16 for requests over 1k tokens or over X concurrent requests.
- Consider separate cost model for Dedicated vs Hosted (reserved GPU pricing -> capex-like amortization).

References and related docs:
- link to existing calibrations in product (notebook path) and quant-sensitivity grid (see linked artifacts)

If you want I can convert this to a 4-tab Google Sheet prototype (inputs / sim / calibration / report) and wire a small script to ingest Redwood Console token distributions for per-customer recommendations.

Action items now:
- Marcus: produce initial speedup table (g5-family) by 2024-11-22
- Leila: run 4 workload evals and share quality deltas by 2024-11-29
- Ravi: synthetic queueing microbench and mapping by 2024-11-26
- Aisha (me): create the sheet prototype and implement core formulas once bench numbers arrive (target 2024-12-05)
